inputs.original_text: Nigeria’s democracy is facing a transformation that is both alarming and largely underexamined: political parties, once intended to be platforms for representation and public service, are increasingly becoming exclusive clubs for the wealthy. The latest developments within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections make this trend painfully clear. The [...]
inputs.modified_text: Look at what we are seeing unfold within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) as they position themselves ahead of the 2027 general elections. It is plain as day that our political parties have been allowed to morph into exclusive clubs for the wealthy. And who pays the price for this decay of traditional standards and civic order? It is the hardworking ordinary citizens and communities who bear the brunt of this instability. Make no mistake, this is a systemic disenfranchisement of everyday people by an elite ruling class that protects its own insular interests at the expense of genuine civic responsibility and structural integrity. Until we restore proper authority and dismantle these entrenched power structures, the vulnerable will continue to be exploited by capital.
